data.title: Strong August employment revives case for Fed hike, TS Lombard says
data.description:
Stronger August employment data had reinforced the underlying uptrend in the U.S. labor market, according to TS Lombard economists led by Dario Perkins.

The analysts said recent weakness in employment growth had likely been noise, with seasonal factors having pulled payroll growth below its underlying trend before August data corrected for that weakness. Upward revisions to July had also helped preserve the broader uptrend, they said.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 162K vs. +55K consensus and +21K in the prior month (revised from -23K), according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday.

The economists pointed to the NFIB survey, which they said generally provided a reliable lead on employment trends, as suggesting that the pickup could continue.

A soft patch remained a risk as the effects of first-quarter tax refunds and a decline in the second-quarter savings rate shifted toward employment and wage growth. But the underlying driver, earnings growth, appeared to be broadening, according to the note.

The report argued that the data did not provide a strong reason for the Federal Reserve to hike rapidly, but that a rate increase this month had become important for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's credibility.

“Hiking this month is a must for credibility,” the economists wrote, arguing that failing to hike would leave Warsh with a difficult situation to address later.

Markets had been pricing what TS Lombard described as a “credibility hike,” a dynamic the economists said was more commonly associated with European central banking.

They cautioned, however, that the U.S. economy had a more flexible labor market and could prove more prone to inflation if growth reaccelerated. Wage growth also appeared to be picking up after excluding lower-signal sectors such as education and health, they said.

The economists said the outlook remained untested and that they saw limited evidence that FOMC members shared their view. As a result, Warsh could have to justify additional hikes in the future if incoming data confirmed the shift.

They also said the muted foreign-exchange reaction to the employment data reinforced their view that a 25-basis-point hike would be reactionary, with markets effectively driving the Fed's policy path.

data.title: U.S. Global investors outlines 7.87% total shareholder yield as fiscal 2026 net income rises to $3.1m
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: U.S. Global Investors (GROW) Q4 2026

Management View

  • Frank Holmes (CEO, Chief Investment Officer & Director) framed the business around product-driven volatility and its link to the stock, saying, “if we're seeing jets going up over 10 days, 6% or down 6% and gold stocks going up or down 9%, well, it shows up in GROW.”
  • Holmes emphasized buybacks and shareholder return mechanics, stating, “the company believes the stock is deeply underbid and therefore, buys back shares when the price is flat or down using an algorithm,” and added that in fiscal 2026 the company “repurchased 733,848 Class A shares using $2 million in cash.”
  • Holmes tied ETF economics to securities lending, saying of JETS, “we made a lot of money for the shareholders in JETS from the securities lending,” while also highlighting the thematic ETF lineup’s positioning around gold, airlines, shipping, and defense.
  • Lisa Callicotte (Chief Financial Officer) reported, “Our average assets under management were $1.53 billion, for the year, and our operating revenues were $10.3 million, and we had a net income of $3.1 million or $0.24 per share.”

Outlook

  • Management did not provide explicit forward EPS, revenue, or AUM guidance in the prepared remarks, focusing instead on positioning and capital allocation.
  • Holmes characterized capital markets opportunity around defense and AI data centers, describing defense spending as “about $2.9 trillion” and saying, “think of a big funnel of money coming, rushing down going into a sector,” while arguing the impact would be “AI related, and that includes data centers.”
  • On capital returns, Holmes said, “We continue to pay this monthly. We've not increased the dividend. We've been more focused on buying back stock in the past few years,” and presented “our overall yield because of the stock buybacks is 7.87%.”

Financial Results

  • Callicotte stated for fiscal year 2026 operating performance, “our operating revenues were $10.3 million for the year, and this is an increase of $1.8 million or 21% from the $8.5 million of revenue in prior year,” attributing it primarily to “increases in asset under management especially in our gold and natural resource funds.”
  • On expense control, Callicotte said, “Operating expenses for the quarter were $10.9 million or 5% lower than prior year,” and added that “operating loss for fiscal year June 30, 2026, was $603,000.”
  • Callicotte highlighted investment-related income, stating, “Other income for the year ended June 30, 2026 was $4.5 million compared to $2.7 million in the prior year,” and said the change was “mainly due to higher unrealized gains in investments.”
  • On balance sheet liquidity, Callicotte said, “We have a net book value of $45.1 million. We have net working capital of $35.7 million and a current ratio of 19.7:1.”

Q&A

  • No analyst Q&A session was included in this transcript.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment could not be assessed because no analyst Q&A was included.
  • Management tone in prepared remarks was slightly positive and valuation-focused, with Holmes saying, “we believe that we're deeply undervalued,” and emphasizing buybacks, dividends, and thematic ETF positioning.
  • Versus the prior quarter’s prepared remarks, the tone remained similarly promotional and macro-driven, with a notable shift toward emphasizing “7.87%” total shareholder yield and fiscal-year results rather than quarterly earnings cadence.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • The current call shifted from Q3’s quarterly financial framing to full-year fiscal 2026 results, with Callicotte now reporting $10.3 million in operating revenues and $3.1 million in net income for the year.
  • Buyback disclosure moved from Q3’s quarterly repurchase detail to a full-year figure, with Holmes reporting 733,848 shares repurchased using $2 million in cash.
  • Shareholder yield messaging changed, with Holmes presenting “7.87%” total yield in Q4 versus Q3’s “9.96%” total shareholder yield reference.
  • Product and macro themes were consistent (gold, airlines, defense/AI), while Q4 added more emphasis on ETF securities lending economics (“we made a lot of money... from the securities lending”) and a new marketing initiative (“Return on Ideas” podcast).

Risks and Concerns

  • Management repeatedly tied earnings and operating results to market variability, with Callicotte noting that operational earnings and investment gains/losses “are also both based on market fluctuations.”
  • Holmes highlighted the company’s business sensitivity to thematic volatility, linking GROW’s stock behavior to large moves in airline- and gold-related exposures.

Final Takeaway

Management presented fiscal 2026 as a year of improved profitability and higher operating revenues tied to higher AUM in gold and natural resources, alongside a continued capital return strategy centered on algorithmic buybacks and an unchanged monthly dividend. Holmes emphasized thematic ETF positioning (gold, airlines, shipping, and defense/AI), pointed to securities lending as an ETF economics lever, and framed shareholder returns through a stated 7.87% total shareholder yield while underscoring that results fluctuate with markets.

data.title: Bybit upgrades Bitcoin staking vault with a 1.2% guaranteed return
data.description:
Bybit, the world’s second-largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, announced that its On-Chain Earn platform has partnered with Function ((FBTC)) to upgrade its Bitcoin (BTC-USD) staking vault, raising the guaranteed annualized return from 0.8% to as much as 1.2%.

According to the PR Newswire, the upgraded product offers eligible Bitcoin holders a fixed 45-day term with no early redemption and a subscription cap of 200 crypto tokens.

At maturity, users can choose automatic renewal, allowing both their principal and accrued returns to roll into the next staking cycle without manual reinvestment.

Bybit said the fixed-return structure gives Bitcoin holders a predictable way to generate yield on idle holdings.

The partnership with Function also expands the company's access to DeFi- and TradFi-related yield opportunities as the exchange looks to provide additional ways for users to put their digital assets to work.

data.title: Tyra Bio rises on upcoming mid-stage trial readout for bladder cancer drug
data.description:
Tyra Biosciences (TYRA) added more than 13% on Thursday, marking its best intraday rally since January, after scheduling a conference call to disclose topline results from a mid-stage trial for its lead candidate, dabogratinib, in bladder cancer.

The Carlsbad, California-based biotech plans to release initial data from its SURF302 Phase 2 study for oral dabogratinib in a conference call scheduled for September 9, 2026, at 8:00 am ET. 

The open-label clinical study is designed to evaluate the FGFR3 inhibitor in two QD doses in patients with intermediate-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

A live webcast of the event along with a slide presentation will be accessible to registered users via the “For Investors" page of the TYRA website, the company said in a statement on Friday.

Previewing the readout, Seeking Alpha analyst Myriam Alvarez, who has a Buy rating on TYRA, wrote in August that SURF302 data, if positive, could validate Tyra’s (TYRA) SNAP drug-design platform, de-risk dabogratinib, and lift the company’s risk-reward profile.

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Strong jobs data, Tesla cybercab scrutiny & more
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages shifted lower after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -0.3%.

Now, here are 3 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

U.S. economy adds 162K jobs: Nonfarm payrolls  grew by 162,000 in August, well above the 55,000 consensus estimate, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 0.3% to $37.75, matching expectations and up 3.1% year-over-year. Prior months were also revised higher, with June and July employment combined now 55,000 above earlier reports. The strong data pushed Fed Watch odds for a 25-basis-point rate hike at the September 16 meeting to 60.2%, up from 50.4% the day before.

Tesla Cybercab launch faces regulatory scrutiny: Tesla  (TSLA) shares  traded lower Friday following a muted Cybercab event in Austin that lacked a livestream, financial details, or an appearance by Elon Musk. Within hours of the launch, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into the vehicle's self-certification, specifically examining its lack of a steering wheel and brake/gas pedals. Barclays analyst Dan Levy called the limited communication "somewhat disappointing," while RBC Capital's Thomas Ito noted the measured rollout pace reflects "an intentional operational strategy rather than any technological constraint" as the company aims to avoid early service failures before expanding to cities like Dallas and Houston.

The Trade Desk cuts 15% of workforce: The Trade Desk (TTD)  announced plans to lay off roughly 15% of its total workforce as part of an organizational restructuring expected to be substantially completed during the third quarter of 2026. The company estimates cash restructuring charges of $39 million to $51 million related to severance and benefits costs, partially offset by a $4 million to $5 million reversal in stock-based compensation. Shares rose approximately 3% in early trading on the news.

data.title: Zscaler dips on Q4 earnings, but analysts see upside in FY27
data.description:
Zscaler (ZS) shares fell about 5% by noon trading on Friday, following fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results that surpassed estimates across the board.

Oppenheimer reiterated its Outperform rating and hefty $250 price target on the cybersecurity stock.

"FY27 guidance issued above consensus, indicating ~60bps of YoY growth above initial expectations," said Oppenheimer analyst Ittai Kidron in an investor note. "Record large deal activity. +$100K/+$1M ARR customer growth accelerated to 19.7%/18.2% YoY, respectively. Security for AI bookings +50% QoQ and relevant pipeline +75% QoQ. Z-Flex adoption is scaling, now at +$770M in bookings (+60% QoQ). Record operating margins. Improving sales productivity. Agentic SecOps launches September 9th."

Meanwhile, Wells Fargo retained its Overweight rating and $210 price target.

"ZS finished the year off well with above-average ARR upside, and a raise to FY27 ARR guidance but was mixed on margin (capex, small restructure)," said Wells Fargo analyst Richard Poland in a note.

However, Seeking Alpha analyst Julia Ostian rated the stock as a Hold. 

"Cybersecurity is on a nice run in the last few months, but there are still companies that are underperforming relative to the overall sector," she said in a Friday analysis. "One of these companies is Zscaler, Inc., and, as a matter of fact, it is underperforming all of the companies the market is widely discussing."

data.title: KNOP outlines $225m refinancing and $113m Hedda Knutsen drop-down as distribution rises to $0.075
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: KNOT Offshore Partners (KNOP) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "Revenues were $96.8 million, operating income $15.6 million, net income $3.4 million, adjusted EBITDA $57.6 million," said (CEO & CFO Derek Lowe), adding that available liquidity was "$143.3 million" as of June 30, 2026.

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) reported operational performance of "96.8% utilization, taking into account scheduled dry docking," and said this was "92.4% utilization overall following the dry docking of Fortaleza."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said KNOP declared "a cash distribution of $0.075 per common unit" paid in August, describing "multiple gradual increases" that are "anchored in our reliable and diversified long-term cash flow and improved balance sheet."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) detailed a post-quarter fleet acquisition: "On September 1, 2026, we purchased the Hedda Knutsen... for a purchase price of $113 million, less an $89.4 million debt facility, plus $0.8 million of capitalized financing fees, resulting in a net cash cost of $24.4 million." He said the deal was negotiated by "our board's independent Conflicts Committee" and noted the vessel is "on time charterer's to Petrobras in Brazil through to November 2034 with an additional 5 years of charter's options."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) highlighted contract and financing actions, including: "the time charter for Hedda Knutsen was executed with Eni to commence in June 2027 for a fixed period of three years plus three charterer's options," and "Time charter for Recife Knutsen was executed by Transpetro to commence in Q3 2026 for a fixed period of two years." He also said KNOP "refinanced" a set of vessels "via a new $225 million 5-year senior secured term-loan facility" at "SOFR plus 165 basis points."

Outlook

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said market conditions in Brazil and the North Sea are tightening, citing "robust multiyear FPSO pipeline, production growth and continuing investment in exploration and existing project expansion," and added that service-volume increases have been "sustained and sufficient to tighten the supply-demand balance, even as new vessels have been delivered."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) reported backlog of "$881.2 million of fixed contracts" at quarter end, and said KNOP is "fully chartered for the remainder of 2026" with "92% firm coverage or 96% including charter's options" in 2027 and "65% firm coverage, or 93%, including charterer's options" in 2028.

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) stated: "we are well advanced in the refinancing of the $65 million facility secured by the Lena Knutsen, which is due later in October."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said KNOP removed two prospective dropdowns: "In June 2026, the partnership decided not to pursue the Frida Knutsen and the Sindre Knutsen and they've been removed from our drop-down inventory."

Financial Results

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) summarized Q2 results as "solid financial results" alongside "strong utilization" and reiterated the quarter’s key figures: revenue of $96.8 million and net income of $3.4 million.

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said liquidity increased versus March 31: "This available liquidity was $2.6 million higher than at March 31," and added that the change was "largely in line with the reducing trend in recent quarters."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) provided borrowing-cost context: "the average margin on our floating rate debt during the second quarter was 2.21% over SOFR."

Q&A

  • Liam Burke, B. Riley Securities, Inc., Research Division: asked whether the Hedda structure implies a different cadence for dropdown growth and whether future dropdown financing could look similar. (CEO & CFO Lowe): "we respond to the offers that are made to us" and said dropdown timing depends on delivery and "the response that the Conflicts Committee wants to make." He added, "the standard model for all of them is that they have a secured debt facility in place already," and said the Hedda debt was "very standard" and that the "$24 million" net cash cost was "fairly consistent" with prior dropdowns.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Slightly positive analyst tone, with limited pressure: Liam Burke opened with "Derek, you've been a busy man this quarter" and focused on mechanics of dropdown cadence and funding rather than challenging results.

  • Management tone was confident and process-driven: (CEO & CFO Lowe) emphasized governance and repeatability of the structure, referencing the "Conflicts Committee" and describing financing as "straightforward" and "very standard" for dropdowns.

  • Versus Q1, the interaction appeared less skeptical and narrower in scope: Q2 featured a single analyst and a single topic (dropdown cadence/financing), while Q1 included multiple analysts pressing on distribution magnitude, macro uncertainty, and revenue movement.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q2 emphasized fleet growth execution and balance sheet actions, led by the Hedda acquisition and the "$225 million" refinancing, whereas Q1 emphasized accounting change: "we changed the useful life estimates of our vessels from 23 years to 20 years" (Q1).

  • Distribution steps accelerated: Q2 declared "$0.075 per common unit" vs. Q1’s "$0.05 per common unit," with Q2 also restating that Q1 was "$0.05" and that it had been "$0.026" for several years before.

  • Backlog and coverage expanded modestly in disclosed figures: Q2 fixed contracts were "$881.2 million" vs. "$858 million" in Q1, with Q2 also providing more explicit 2027–2028 coverage percentages.

  • Analyst focus narrowed in Q2 to dropdown financing repeatability, while Q1 analysts pressed for distribution “magnitude” and asked about macro and fleet aging; management in Q1 declined to provide distribution specifics, while Q2 focused on standardized dropdown mechanics.

Risks and Concerns

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) flagged refinancing execution timing as a near-term item: "we are well advanced in the refinancing of the $65 million facility secured by the Lena Knutsen, which is due later in October."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) framed forward coverage as reliant on option exercise, stating: "Based on current charter rates, we believe charter options are likely to be exercised given the strength of the charter market."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) noted utilization was affected by planned off-hire: Q2 utilization included "scheduled dry docking" and specifically referenced "the dry docking of Fortaleza."

Final Takeaway

KNOP’s management presented Q2 2026 as a quarter of steady utilization and contracted cash flows, followed by a material post-quarter fleet addition through the Hedda Knutsen dropdown that management said extends contract runway into 2034 with additional options. Alongside a $225 million refinancing at SOFR plus 165 basis points and an October refinancing in progress for a $65 million facility, Derek Lowe repeatedly framed dropdown execution and financing as standardized and governance-led via the Conflicts Committee, while continuing the stated plan of multiple gradual distribution increases, marked this quarter by a $0.075 per-unit payout.

data.title: Infleqtion initiated with Buy rating due to its full-stack quantum platform: B. Riley
data.description:
B. Riley Securities initiated coverage of Infleqtion (INFQ) with a Buy rating and $23 price target, as it is one of only two publicly traded quantum stocks with a full-stack platform.

Shares inched up 1% during Friday trading.

"We view the entity as one of just two publicly traded quantum names presenting a full-stack platform play with multiple product groups plus an optimized software stack, alongside IonQ (IONQ)," said B. Riley analysts Craig Ellis and Rebecca Zamsky in an investor note.

B. Riley has a Buy rating and $100 price target on IonQ.

"We like an advantaged technology position, as neutral-atom all-to-all gate connectivity lends high logical qubit efficiency and error correction to lift our confidence that already commercial sensing products can add compute systems in a few years," Ellis said of Infleqtion. "Because the same physics underpins sensors and clocks today and likely compute systems ahead, leverage prospects seem compelling inside a large and growing TAM, rising to $16.5B and $35B-$80B in 2030E and 2035E, respectively, with our CY28 and CY29 revenue estimates rising to $75M and $90M."

Infleqtion hit the New York Stock Exchange in mid-February. It has since traded between $8 and $21.  

"Continued volatile sector share action, which often seemingly amplifies AI sentiment, is presenting attractive entry points, in our view, into a steady stream of potential 12-month fundamental and financial catalysts as the industry races toward commercial workload uptake in a few years, which we believe will eventually span all industries," Ellis added. "While early-stage valuation is tricky and with numerous risks to navigate, we believe INFQ has the right ingredients and potential execution to be a long-term quantum winner."

Last week, Infleqtion was awarded a $20M contract from NASA. The follow-on contract is for the continued development of the Quantum Gravity Gradiometer Pathfinder, which is being led by NASA JPL. The Pathfinder is designed to fly the world's first space-based quantum gravity sensor.

data.title: PayPal pauses sale of venture capital portfolio arm - Axios Pro
data.description:
PayPal (PYPL) has paused the planned sale of its venture capital portfolio from ~$900 million to $1 billion.

Offers are said to have come in lower than expected, with the highest bids around 60 cents on the dollar, according to an Axios Pro report on Thursday, which cited multiple unidentified sources. PayPal may have decided that the timing of the sale wasn't ideal, with fintech valuations at depressed levels. 

The update comes after PayPal (PYPL) earlier this year decided to wind down its corporate venture arm, hiring Jefferies to advise on a possible sale. Investments in the portfolio include shopping app Tabby and crypto platform Anchorage.

“As part of our continued efforts to sharpen our focus, we are exploring strategic options for our corporate venture capital arm, PayPal Ventures,” a company spokesperson said in a statement to Fortune in June. 

Shares of PayPal fell 3% on Friday, largely erasing Thursday's 4% gain amid renewed takeover speculation.
